articles.title: GPT-6.1 Sol
articles.content:
We’re introducingGPT-6.1 Sol, an upgrade to GPT-6 Sol that nearly matches GPT-6 Astra’s intelligence on agentic coding, computer use, and professional work at one-fifth of Astra’s standard input and output token prices. Cached input costs just$0.10 per million tokens—95% less than standard input pricing and 50% less than GPT-6 Sol’s cached input pricing—giving developers more room to build and run capable agents that reuse context across requests.

Our most intelligent model for the
best results.

Near-Astra intelligence for a fifth of the price.

Fast and efficient everyday work
at scale.

GPT-6.1 Sol offers a new balance of capability and cost for important everyday work. It delivers substantial improvements over GPT-6 Sol across complex professional tasks, from writing and debugging code to understanding documents and executing multi-step business workflows. On several of these evaluations, it approaches GPT-6 Astra’s performance at substantially lower cost.

OnDeepSWE v1.1, which evaluates complex software-engineering tasks in real codebases, GPT-6.1 Sol matches GPT-6 Astra at roughly one-fifth of the cost, while eclipsing GPT-6 Sol’s best score by 6.4 percentage points at a lower reasoning effort and cost.

InDeepSWE 1.1⁠⁠(opens in a new window), AI agents solve original, long-horizon software engineering tasks.

OnGDP.pdf, which measures how accurately models answer professional questions using complex PDF documents, including tables, charts, diagrams, and fine-print details, GPT-6.1 Sol scores higher than Opus 5.5 with fallbacks at less than half the cost per task across the tested reasoning settings. It also approaches GPT-6 Astra’s state-of-the-art performance at roughly one-fifth the cost per task.

InGDP.pdf⁠(opens in a new window), models must answer real-world prompts about complex PDFs pulled from professional workflows in finance, healthcare, legal, and seven other professional domains.

OnAutomationBench, which measures whether agents correctly complete multi-step business workflows, GPT-6.1 Sol scores 2.2 percentage points above Opus 5.5 at medium reasoning effort, at roughly a third of the cost. That score is also up 4.8 percentage points from GPT-6 Sol at the same setting.

InAutomationBench 1.0.6⁠⁠(opens in a new window), AI agents are tested on end-to-end workflows using 47 tools across sales, marketing, operations, support, finance, and HR. The datapoint for Claude Fable 5.1 understates its actual cost, as it omits the cost of fallbacks, which occurred on ~40% of tasks.

GPT-6.1 Sol also makes substantial progress on tasks that require interacting with computer applications. OnOSWorld 2.0’s offline set, which evaluates agents on demanding computer-use workflows, GPT-6.1 Sol outperforms GPT-6 Sol by seven percentage points at maximum reasoning effort at less than half the cost. It comes within 2.1 percentage points of Astra’s score at maximum reasoning effort at roughly one-seventh the cost per task.

InOSWorld 2.0⁠⁠(opens in a new window), AI agents attempt long-horizon computer-use workflows spanning everyday and professional tasks. We report the partial reward on the offline set from the v2026.08.08 release.

OnTerminal-Bench Science 0.1, which evaluates scientific workflows including data analysis, simulation, and theorem proving, GPT-6.1 Sol more than doubles GPT-6 Sol’s score at maximum reasoning effort at less than half the cost per task. At maximum effort, GPT-6.1 Sol costs $5.47 per task on average, compared with $23.21 for Opus 5.5 and $23.80 for Astra, delivering substantial scientific capability at over 75% lower cost than either model.

GPT-6 Astra still achieves the highest score among the models tested at 68.1%, and should be used for the most difficult scientific research tasks.

InTerminal-Bench Science 0.1⁠(opens in a new window), agents complete scientific research workflows using code and terminal tools, including analyzing data, running simulations, and fitting models.

GPT-6.1 Sol also improves factual accuracy on difficult prompts. Its largest factuality improvement over GPT-6 Sol comes at low reasoning effort, where it reduces the share of responses containing a factual error from 11.4% to 7.7%—a reduction of approximately 32%. Across the tested reasoning settings, its error rate remains within 1.9 percentage points of GPT-6 Astra’s, at less than one-fifth the cost per task.

This evaluation measures the share of answers containing at least one factual error on de-identified conversations where users flagged an earlier model’s error. These deliberately difficult prompts are not representative of typical usage.

We evaluate factuality on de-identified ChatGPT conversations where users had flagged a factual error from a prior model. These error-inducing conversations are not representative of typical usage, where factual errors are more rare.

GPT-6.1 Sol shows substantial improvements over GPT-6 Sol in our alignment evaluations, bringing it closer to GPT-6 Astra.

GPT-6.1 Sol is more transparent about its limitations and more reliable at respecting user intent and safety constraints. In challenging evaluations, it shows lower failure rates than GPT-6 Sol on transparency about broken search tools, respecting explicit restrictions, and avoiding unauthorized outcomes during agentic tasks. We observed no attempts to bypass an automated safety reviewer, matching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Sol. Full details can be found in theGPT-6.1 Sol system card addendum⁠(opens in a new window).

The evaluations below deliberately test challenging situations and do not measure failure rates in typical use.

GPT-6.1 Sol is available starting today to all Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex. GPT-6.1 Sol is not yet available in Chat. Developers can also access it through the OpenAI API as gpt-6.1-sol. Its standard API prices are $2 per million input tokens, $0.10 per million cached input tokens, and $10 per million output tokens. In the coming days, we’ll also offer GPT-6.1 SolUltrafast⁠, with up to 8x faster token generation compared to its standard speed in Codex.

Evaluations of GPT were performed in our research environment or via our API, which may provide slightly different output from production ChatGPT due to differences in the system prompts, tools available, efforts, etc. Evaluations of competitor models were taken from publicly available reports.

articles.summary: OpenAI는 에이전트 코딩, 컴퓨터 사용, 전문 업무에서 GPT-6 Astra에 근접한 성능을 목표로 하는 GPT-6.1 Sol을 발표했다. 회사에 따르면 표준 입력·출력 토큰 가격은 Astra의 5분의 1이며, 캐시된 입력은 100만 토큰당 0.10달러다. DeepSWE v1.1에서는 약 5분의 1 비용으로 Astra와 동등한 성능을 기록했고, 복잡한 PDF 기반 전문 질의 평가에서도 Astra에 근접했다고 밝혔다. 반복적으로 문맥을 재사용하는 업무용 에이전트의 비용 절감 가능성이 크지만, 제시된 성능과 비용 비교는 회사가 공개한 평가 조건에 한정된다.

articles.title: Google Open-Sources Harness2, a Recursive Agent Harnessing Framework
articles.content: Google Cloud AI Research has open-sourced Harness². It is a recursive agent harnessing framework that improves the code and files around a frozen model. For developers, the pitch is simple. Your agent may get better without a better model. TL;DR Size: A framework, not a model. 0 parameters trained; 8 editable harness components. Version 0.1.0. Runs on: Linux with Python 3.12 or 3.13 and uv. Model runs call models through Vertex AI. GPU requirement: Not disclosed. Performance: 1 refinement step improved all 4 model and harness setups on all 3 benchmarks. Best: GLM-5 under OpenCode rose from 64.2 to 75.7 on WorkBuddy-Bench (+11.5 points). Worst: GLM-5 under Codex gained only 1.2 points on JobBench (23.6 to 24.8). What is Harness²? Harness² is a plug-and-play framework from Google Research that refines an agent’s harness during deployment. A harness is everything around the model: prompts, tools, memory, skills and orchestration. Harnessing is the process of optimizing that system. Model weights never change. The target setting is the open world. Tasks arrive unseen, and no verifier says whether an answer is right. The research team argues that most self-improvement methods assume labels or test cases. Harness² is built to work without them. What are the 8 harness components? Harness² exposes 8 editable components, each mounted as a file: System prompt Guardrails Memory Tool guidance Subagents Skills Scripts Plugins (middleware) They cover context construction, the tool interface, delegation and behavior inside the tool loop. The layout extends the 7-file split from earlier Agentic Harness Engineering work by 1 component. How does recursive agent harnessing work? The framework runs two linked levels of recursion: Task-level recursion uses a contrastive Propose, Probe, Compose step. First, the agent runs the task once with the base harness. An editor then proposes 2 candidates. The invariant candidate targets general agent failures such as planning or tool use. The domain candidate targets knowledge and procedures for the current domain. Both candidates run on the same task. The composer compares their trajectories against the reference and keeps only edits backed by observed behavior. Harnessing-level recursion happens after each task. A reflector stores the adopted harness plus an EXPERIENCE.md file of lessons. This library guides future proposals. Each new task still starts from the base harness. The budget k scales the search. Parallel mode probes k invariant and k domain candidates, then makes k compositions. Sequential mode chains k refinement steps. articles.summary: Google Cloud AI Research가 모델 가중치를 바꾸지 않고 에이전트 주변의 코드와 파일을 개선하는 오픈소스 프레임워크 Harness²를 공개했다. 시스템 프롬프트, 가드레일, 메모리, 도구 지침 등 8개 구성 요소를 수정하며, 정답 라벨이나 검증기가 없는 배포 환경을 겨냥한다. 기사에 따르면 한 차례 개선만으로 4개 모델·하네스 조합 모두가 3개 벤치마크에서 향상됐고, GLM-5와 OpenCode 조합은 WorkBuddy-Bench에서 64.2점에서 75.7점으로 올랐다. 모델 재학습 없이 에이전트 성능을 개선할 수 있다는 점이 중요하지만, 일부 조합의 향상 폭은 1.2점에 그쳐 효과는 환경별로 달랐다.

articles.title: Meet Voxel51 3.0: A Unified Multimodal Data Platform for Physical AI
articles.content: Voxel51 has released Voxel51 3.0, a very important update to its data platform. Voxel51 3.0 is an end-to-end multimodal data platform that puts search, curation, annotation and evaluation in one system. It targets teams training models on sensor data from robots, vehicles and factories. The release adds Voxel51 Agent, a data provenance layer and free self-service access. TL;DR Scale: Voxel51 Agent ships with 45+ MCP tools, 80+ operators and 18 open-source skills. Runs on: Hosted web app at app.voxel51.com, or self-hosted in cloud, hybrid, on-prem and air-gapped setups. No local GPU requirement disclosed. Performance: No product benchmarks published. Voxel51 cites its own survey data instead. Best: Free tier includes Voxel51 Agent, 30,000 inference requests and 30 compute hours per month. Worst: Free tier caps at 3 datasets of 10,000 samples each and 20 GB of storage. What is new in Voxel51 3.0? Voxel51 3.0 expands the platform beyond its roots in visual data with 3 core additions. Time-series multimodal support: Teams can view multiple sensor streams on 1 timeline. Segment-level embeddings find specific moments inside long recordings. Unified annotation: Labeling covers 2D, 3D, video and multimodal data. It includes automated QA, annotator metrics and human-in-the-loop review. Agentic Labeling: Vision-language models generate labels from natural-language instructions and examples. Supported modalities include MCAP, images, video, 3D point clouds, meshes, DICOM, NIfTI, geospatial data and audio. How does Voxel51 Search work? Voxel51 Search is a persistent hybrid index. It indexes datasets and computes embeddings automatically, so search works from day 1. Semantic retrieval finds visually or semantically similar moments, even without shared labels. Lexical and structured queries handle exact terms, timestamps, sensor fields and metadata. Embeddings and structured fields stay in native form and are combined at retrieval time. Vector retrieval runs on LanceDB. It supports vector, scalar and full-text indexes, and separates storage from compute. Teams choose what to embed, which model and compute to use, and when. Incremental updates avoid full rebuilds when samples arrive or schemas change. What can Voxel51 Agent do? Voxel51 Agent chains search, curation, annotation and evaluation into repeatable workflows. Example workflows: A robotics team searches behaviors across thousands of episodes, then curates balanced training sets. A perception team starts from a model failure and pulls similar long-tail scenarios for labeling. The agent can also write code to build custom plugins. All workflows inherit the organization’s permissions and governance controls. How does data provenance work in Voxel51 3.0? Voxel51 3.0 adds 4 provenance layers: Deployment-level activity log: who did what, and when, across the deployment. Dataset-level activity log: how a single dataset evolved. Sample-level edit history: label, metadata and property changes per sample. Dataset versioning: immutable snapshots to reproduce training and evaluation runs. Events flow through fiftyone-mq for job scheduling and Activity Core for event tracking. Can teams bring their own models? Yes. The platform is model-agnostic across embeddings, auto-labeling, inference and evaluation. A team can bootstrap with a foundation model, then swap in its own domain model. Why does Voxel51 argue data work decides outcomes? Voxel51 cites its 2026 State of Physical AI survey. 58% of “exceptional” teams spend more than half their project time on data work. Only 21% of struggling teams do the same. This is vendor-run research, so read it as directional. && How does Voxel51 3.0 compare with Encord and Foxglove? FeatureVoxel51 3.0EncordFoxgloveCore focusSearch, curate, annotate, evaluate multimodal dataAnnotation, curation and data managementRobotics visualization, observability and data managementFree tier3 datasets, 10,000 samples each, 20 GBNot disclosed10 GB storage, 3 users, 5 devicesPaid entryTeam: 8 seats, 2,800 compute hrs/mo (price not disclosed)Starter (price not disclosed)Pro: $20/mo + usage, 1 TB storageBuilt-in agentVoxel51 AgentData agents (Team plan)Agent sidebarMCP45+ MCP toolsNot disclosedFoxglove MCP (local MCP on paid plans)SearchHybrid semantic, lexical and metadataMulti-modal search, querying, filteringSemantic Search (beta) plus structured searchAnnotation2D, 3D, video, multimodal, Agentic LabelingImage, video, audio, documents; 3D and LiDAR add-onEvents on time segmentsTime-series sensor dataMCAP, synced streams, segment embeddingsSensor streams (see note)MCAP, ROS 1, ROS 2 nativeProvenanceActivity logs, edit history, versioningNot disclosedAudit logs (not on Free)Self-hostedOn-prem and air-gapped availableVPC and on-prem (add-on or Enterprise)Self-hosted data on Enterprise; BYO storage on Pro Encord’s sensor-stream support is stated in its Series C release. Prices verified October 17, 2026. Key Takeaways Voxel51 3.0 merges search, curation, annotation and evaluation in 1 platform. Voxel51 Agent ships with 45+ MCP tools, 80+ operators and 18 skills. Activity logs, edit history and versioning make training data traceable. Free tier: 3 datasets, 10,000 samples each, no credit card. Check out the official blog post, the press release and the Voxel51 docs, or try it at app.voxel51.com. All credit goes to the researcher of this project. Also, feel free to follow us on Twitter and don’t forget to join our 150k+ML SubReddit and Subscribe to our Newsletter. Wait! are you on telegram? now you can join us on telegram as well. articles.summary: Voxel51은 로봇·차량·공장 센서 데이터의 검색, 선별, 주석, 평가를 통합한 멀티모달 데이터 플랫폼 Voxel51 3.0을 출시했다. 여러 센서 스트림을 하나의 타임라인에서 확인하고 구간 단위 임베딩으로 긴 기록의 특정 순간을 찾을 수 있으며, 비전언어모델을 활용한 라벨 생성과 데이터 이력 관리도 추가했다. Voxel51 Agent는 45개 이상의 MCP 도구를 제공하고, 플랫폼은 호스팅 서비스뿐 아니라 온프레미스와 망분리 환경도 지원한다. 물리적 환경에서 작동하는 AI의 데이터 작업을 통합할 수 있으나, 제품 성능 벤치마크는 공개되지 않았고 무료 요금제에는 데이터셋과 저장 공간 제한이 있다.

articles.title: How to Make Zero-Training Tabular Predictions with NVIDIA Structured Data Models
articles.content:
In this tutorial, we implement Structured Data Models, NVIDIA’s new library that puts several pretrained foundation models for tables behind one PyTorch interface, and use it to make predictions without training. The library wraps TabICLv2 and KumoTabular for single tables and KumoRelational for whole relational databases, and each of them answers by in-context learning: we hand the model a set of labeled rows and the rows we want predicted, and it returns probabilities or a full predictive distribution in one forward pass. We start with the library’s typed table tensors, compare the two tabular models against trained scikit-learn baselines, reuse an encoded context across many queries, read calibrated prediction intervals off a regression, and scale to twenty classes. We then look at the places where the defaults quietly do the wrong thing: a preprocessing recipe that drops timestamp and text columns and an explainer with two traps in it, before building a small three-table shop database and predicting customer activity from it directly, including the one argument that separates an honest relational model from a leaky one. articles.summary: NVIDIA의 Structured Data Models 라이브러리는 사전학습된 표·관계형 데이터 모델을 하나의 PyTorch 인터페이스로 제공한다. TabICLv2와 KumoTabular는 단일 표를, KumoRelational은 관계형 데이터베이스를 다루며, 라벨이 있는 행과 예측 대상 행을 입력하는 인컨텍스트 학습으로 별도 학습 없이 예측한다. 튜토리얼은 문맥 인코딩 재사용, 회귀 예측 구간, 다중 클래스 분류와 여러 표를 연결한 예측을 소개한다. 표 데이터 예측의 구현 부담을 줄일 수 있지만, 기본 전처리에서 시간·텍스트 열이 제외되는 문제와 관계형 예측의 데이터 누출 위험을 점검해야 한다.

articles.title: LG CNS, 글로벌 디지털 워크플레이스 평가서 국내 첫 ‘메이저 플레이어’ 선정
articles.content:
LG CNS(대표 현신균)가 글로벌 시장조사기관 IDC의 디지털 워크플레이스 서비스 평가에서 국내 기업 최초로 ‘메이저 플레이어’에 선정됐다. 에이전틱 인공지능(AI)을 활용해 정보 검색과 업무 보조를 넘어 실제 업무 실행까지 자동화하는 플랫폼 역량과 금융·공공·제조 등 보안 요구 수준이 높은 산업에서 쌓은 사업 경험이 글로벌 경쟁력으로 인정받았다.

LG CNS는 IDC의 ‘2026년 전 세계 디지털 워크플레이스 서비스 벤더 평가’에서 메이저 플레이어로 선정됐다고 19일 밝혔다. 이번 평가에는 타타컨설턴시서비스(TCS), 인포시스, NTT 데이터, 코그니전트, 델, HP 등 글로벌 IT 기업 18곳이 포함됐으며, LG CNS는 평가에 참여한 국내 기업 가운데 유일하게 이름을 올렸다.

IDC 마켓스케이프는 IT 기업의 현재 사업 역량과 미래 전략을 종합적으로 분석하는 평가 모델이다. 제품과 서비스 경쟁력뿐 아니라 고객 사례와 실제 이용 경험 등을 함께 살펴본다. 디지털 워크플레이스 서비스는 PC와 스마트 오피스 기기, 통합 커뮤니케이션·협업 환경 등을 기획·구축·운영·지원하는 분야로, 최근에는 AI와 자동화를 활용해 업무 환경 관리와 생산성을 개선하는 역량이 중요해지고 있다.

이번 평가에서 LG CNS의 핵심 경쟁력으로 꼽힌 것은 업무혁신 에이전틱 AI 서비스 ‘에이엑스씽크(a)’를 중심으로 한 디지털 워크플레이스 플랫폼이다. 에이전틱 AI는 사용자의 지시와 목표를 바탕으로 필요한 작업을 계획하고 실행하는 AI 기술이다. LG CNS는 이를 기업 업무 환경에 적용해 단순한 질의응답이나 정보 제공을 넘어 실제 업무 처리까지 지원하는 서비스를 제공하고 있다.

에이엑스씽크는 기업 업무 포털과 그룹웨어 ‘웍스(Worx)’, 모바일 업무 포털·그룹웨어 ‘웍스 엠(Worx M)’, 개인용 AI 에이전트 ‘클로(Claw)’, AI 통번역·회의 지원 서비스 ‘트랜슬레이터(Translator)’, AI 문서 작성 서비스 ‘독(Doc)’ 등으로 구성된다. 업무 포털과 문서 작성, 회의 지원 등 기업에서 자주 사용하는 기능에 AI를 접목해 직원들이 여러 도구를 오가며 처리하던 업무를 보다 통합적으로 수행하도록 지원하는 것이 특징이다.

IDC는 LG CNS의 강점으로 AI 네이티브 플랫폼 역량과 규제 산업 및 보안·망분리 환경에 대한 전문성, 고객 검증을 거친 엔드투엔드 사업 수행 역량을 제시했다. 특히 금융·공공·제조 등 엄격한 보안과 규제 요건을 충족해야 하는 환경에서 에이전틱 AI 사업 경험을 축적했다는 점을 주요 경쟁력으로 평가했다.

IDC 보고서는 전통적인 디지털 워크플레이스 서비스를 넘어 에이전트 기반 업무 실행으로 전환하려는 기업이 혁신 파트너로 LG CNS를 고려할 수 있다고 평가했다. 컨설팅부터 시스템 구축과 운영까지 전 과정을 아우르는 사업 역량, 고객의 비즈니스 환경과 산업에 대한 이해, 유연한 대응과 협업 방식, 에이전틱 AI 전문 인력도 고객 평가에서 긍정적으로 언급됐다.

실제 적용 성과도 제시됐다. LG CNS는 에이엑스씽크를 비롯한 디지털 워크플레이스 서비스를 미국과 중국, 싱가포르, 독일 등 LG 계열사의 해외 사업장에 적용해 업무 생산성이 20~40% 향상되는 효과를 확인했다고 밝혔다. 업무시간 단축에 따른 생산성 개선과 외산 솔루션 도입 대비 라이선스 비용 절감 등을 종합하면 연간 수백억원 규모의 비용 절감 효과가 발생할 것으로 추산했다.

김홍근 LG CNS 디지털비즈니스사업부장(부사장)은 “이번 IDC ‘메이저 플레이어’ 선정은 에이엑스씽크를 중심으로 차별화해온 디지털 워크플레이스 서비스 경쟁력을 글로벌 시장에서 인정받았다는 점에서 의미가 크다”며 “앞으로도 에이전틱 AI를 기반으로 고객의 업무 생산성을 혁신하고 시장에서 입지를 더욱 강화해 나갈 것”이라고 말했다.

이번 선정은 디지털 업무 환경의 경쟁 기준이 기존 시스템의 구축과 운영을 넘어 AI가 업무를 직접 수행하는 단계로 이동하고 있음을 보여준다. 기업용 AI 도입의 성과를 좌우하는 요소도 모델 성능만이 아니라 기존 업무 시스템과의 연계, 보안 및 접근권한 관리, 실제 업무 흐름에 대한 이해로 확장되고 있다. LG CNS가 해외 사업장에서 제시한 생산성 개선 효과를 다양한 산업과 고객 환경에서도 재현할 수 있을지가 향후 글로벌 시장에서 경쟁력을 넓히는 관건이 될 전망이다.
articles.summary: LG CNS는 IDC의 2026년 전 세계 디지털 워크플레이스 서비스 평가에서 국내 기업 최초로 ‘메이저 플레이어’에 선정됐다고 밝혔다. 핵심 플랫폼인 에이엑스씽크는 업무 포털, 그룹웨어, 개인용 AI 에이전트, 통번역·회의 지원, 문서 작성을 통합해 정보 검색을 넘어 업무 실행을 지원한다. 기사에 따르면 IDC는 AI 네이티브 플랫폼과 금융·공공·제조 분야의 보안·망분리 환경 경험을 강점으로 평가했다. LG CNS는 해외 계열사 사업장 적용으로 생산성이 20~40% 향상됐다고 밝혔으며, 연간 수백억원 규모의 비용 절감은 회사의 추산이다.

articles.title: TinyFish Makes Search Free: What It Really Costs an AI Agent to Read the Web
articles.content: An AI agent that reads the web pays 2 kinds of cost. The first is the retrieval charge: what a search or fetch API bills per request. The second is model processing: content passed from retrieved pages into an AI model consumes tokens, while reasoning and generated responses add further costs. TinyFish, a web infrastructure company for AI agents, argues that teams budget for the model and underestimate how much retrieved content drives it. This article walks through the token math, the context-window impact, and what the Artificial Analysis Search API leaderboard does and does not show. TL;DR What it runs on: TinyFish uses a web-native AI model designed for search, retrieval, and interaction with live websites. The model runs on TinyFish-managed infrastructure, while its cloud browser fleet renders pages and handles website interactions. No local GPU is needed. Access is via REST, Python and TypeScript SDKs, CLI or MCP. Performance: On the Sep 28, 2026 Artificial Analysis snapshot, TinyFish Search (web) scores 71 at $9.30 per 1,000 benchmark tasks, with 59.0 seconds per task (model plus search time). Best: $0 retrieval charge within rate limits (Search: 30 requests/min, 500/hour; Fetch: 150 URLs/min, 1,000/day), and the lowest total cost among the 12 configurations displayed on the leaderboard. Trade-offs: The second longest time per task among displayed configurations, and an Agent product whose built-in model cannot be swapped. Scores: Highest displayed is Perplexity Search (medium) at 80. Lowest displayed is TinyFish Search (web) at 71. The no-search baseline is 33. Retrieval charges vs model processing costs Search and fetch APIs usually bill per request or per page. Whatever they return then enters the model’s context and is billed as input tokens. Reasoning and output tokens come on top. Enterprises now route each task to the cheapest capable model, a trend underlined when Stripe agreed to acquire OpenRouter, a gateway spanning 400+ models from 80+ providers. Routing lowers the price per token. It does not change how many tokens a retrieved page contains. Free Search and Fetch remove TinyFish’s retrieval charge within its limits. The downstream model still incurs inference costs. That is why the size of each returned page matters. How big is one page in tokens? TinyFish ran a fetch quality evaluation on June 2, 2026, across 45 URLs and 5 providers on default settings. For one Daily Mail article with a body of roughly 4,300 characters, the providers returned: ProviderCharacters returnedEst. tokens*Input cost at $1 / 1M tokens*TinyFish Fetch4,737~1,184~$0.00118Exa Contents65,793~16,448~$0.01645Firecrawl Scrape171,095~42,774~$0.04277Tavily Extract46,433~11,608~$0.01161Parallel Extract600 (excerpt, not the article)~150~$0.00015 *Marktechpost calculation: ~4 characters per token and an illustrative input price of $1 per 1M tokens. Input processing only; excludes retrieval charges, reasoning and output. Real counts vary by tokenizer. Character counts from TinyFish’s evaluation. In this example, Firecrawl returned approximately 36 times as many characters as TinyFish.  Parallel also returned only an excerpt rather than the complete article, so its smaller output is not directly comparable to the full-page extractions. While this illustrates how extraction output size can affect token consumption, the difference comes from a single webpage and should not be generalized across all websites. Those percentages are not used for this individual page comparison because outputs above 30,000 characters were truncated before judging. Context limits and repeated calls Assume every extracted character goes into the same context, with no filtering, truncation or summarization. A page containing approximately 42,774 tokens would consume about one-third of a 128K-token context window. Three such pages would require approximately 128,322 tokens, leaving little or no room for system instructions, conversation history, or the agent’s response. Agent loops also resend context. Artificial Analysis notes that each turn resends the full conversation, with earlier input billed at the model’s cached-input price. Caching lowers the cost of rereading a noisy page. It does not remove it, and the page still occupies the window. In that TinyFish internal evaluation, a result counted as covered only with at least 1,000 characters and a judged signal ratio above 30%. Coverage was TinyFish 93%, Tavily 80%, Exa 73%, Firecrawl 62% and Parallel 58%. Among usable results only, median signal was 90.5% for TinyFish and 89.7% for Exa. TinyFish ran the test on itself, the sample is 45 URLs, and news pages drove most of the gap. Why TinyFish makes retrieval free TinyFish frames search as one operation inside execution, like DNS or storage for ordinary software. An agent booking, comparing or filling out a form should care whether the job got done, not which search system found the page.  TinyFish attributes its free retrieval pricing to three aspects of its infrastructure: Shared infrastructure: TinyFish built its browser fleet, stealth systems, session hydration and elastic scaling before Search was a product. TinyFish says this changes the marginal economics of search. It does not make the infrastructure free to run. Specialized models: TinyFish says its web-native AI model is designed for search, fetch, and live-site interaction. Its development draws on agent operational trajectories and large volumes of search activity, helping reduce reliance on general-purpose models for intermediate web tasks. No giant index: TinyFish says it would rather learn how work gets done than become an indexing company. TinyFish charges separately for Agent and Browser usage, while Search and Fetch remain free within their published limits. Per the pricing page, Search is free at 30 requests per minute and 500 per hour. Fetch is free at 150 URLs per minute and 1,000 per day. Both keep working at a $0 Wallet balance. Agent costs $0.016 per step with 2 concurrent runs, and Browser costs $0.002 per minute with 5 sessions. New accounts get $8 in Wallet funds. What the benchmark shows, and what it does not Artificial Analysis holds the answer model fixed (GPT-5.6 Luna, medium) and changes only the search provider. Model cost covers input, cached, reasoning and output tokens. Differences between providers reflect returned payloads, how many searches the model runs and how much it reasons. On the Sep 28, 2026 snapshot, model cost ranges from $8.04 to $21.65 per 1,000 tasks across the 12 displayed configurations. These come from 26 products across 13 providers. TinyFish posts $0 for search plus $9.30 for the model, the lowest displayed total. The trade-offs: TinyFish recorded a Search Index score of 71, the lowest among the displayed configurations, and a DeepSearchQA F1 of 67. Its benchmark time was approximately 59 seconds per task, combining estimated model processing time and measured search time rather than representing API latency alone. Because Artificial Analysis uses its own shared extraction layer, the results do not directly measure TinyFish Fetch. Similarly, benchmark costs per 1,000 tasks should not be confused with API prices per 1,000 requests, since a single task may involve multiple searches. Key Takeaways Agents pay retrieval charges plus model processing on everything retrieved. articles.summary: TinyFish는 정해진 호출 한도 안에서 검색·페이지 가져오기 요금을 받지 않는 웹 접근 서비스를 제공하며, REST와 SDK, CLI, MCP를 지원한다. 기사는 검색 API 요금과 별도로 검색 결과를 모델에 입력하고 추론하는 토큰 비용이 발생하므로, 무료 검색이 전체 에이전트 비용의 무료화를 뜻하지는 않는다고 설명한다. 2026년 9월 28일 Artificial Analysis 평가에서 TinyFish Search는 71점과 1,000개 작업당 9.30달러를 기록해 표시된 12개 구성 중 총비용이 가장 낮았지만 점수도 가장 낮았다. 작업당 시간은 59초로 두 번째로 길었고 Agent 제품의 내장 모델은 교체할 수 없어, 비용과 속도·유연성 사이의 절충이 필요하다.

articles.title: Disney agrees to hire the majority of Character.AI’s workforce
articles.content: The filing also says that the “vast majority” of Character.AI employees who were offered jobs at Disney accepted them. However, this is a stalking horse bid, so another company could come forward with a higher offer.
articles.summary: Disney가 Character.AI 인력의 과반을 채용하기로 합의했다고 보도됐다. 제출 문서에 따르면 Disney로부터 채용 제안을 받은 직원의 ‘대다수’가 이를 수락했다. 다만 이번 제안은 다른 입찰의 기준이 되는 스토킹 호스 입찰이므로 더 높은 제안이 나올 수 있으며, 인력 이동의 최종 결과와 구체적인 기술·제품 통합 계획은 제공된 자료만으로 확인되지 않는다.

articles.title: Anthropic says it’s committing 5% of its shares to a ‘public benefit fund’
articles.content: Anthropic said that it will commit 5% of its shares to the fund.
articles.summary: Anthropic은 자사 주식의 5%를 ‘공익 기금’에 배정하겠다고 밝혔다. AI 기업의 지분을 공익 목적 재원으로 연결하는 계획이라는 점에서 의미가 있다. 다만 제공된 자료에는 기금의 운영 구조, 수혜 대상, 집행 시점이 없어 실제 공익 효과와 이행 방식은 판단하기 어렵다.

articles.title: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns
articles.content: A Meta spokesperson insisted that the updated terms did not reflect a change in the way Meta crawls the web.
articles.summary: Meta가 웹 스크래핑과 AI 학습 관련 우려를 불러일으킨 약관 문구를 삭제했다고 보도됐다. Meta 대변인은 수정된 약관이 회사의 웹 크롤링 방식 변경을 의미하지는 않는다고 강조했다. 약관 표현의 수정과 실제 데이터 수집 관행의 변화는 구분해야 하며, 제공된 자료만으로 AI 학습용 데이터 이용 범위가 달라졌다고 단정할 수 없다.

articles.title: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings
articles.content: The composition of Anthropic’s workforce and the type of work getting done have changed significantly in the past year.
articles.summary: Anthropic은 지난 1년 동안 인력 구성과 수행 업무의 유형이 크게 달라졌다고 밝혔다. 보도 제목에 따르면 주니어 인력의 비중이 낮아지고 회의에 쓰는 시간이 늘었다. AI 기업 내부의 조직·업무 방식 변화를 보여주는 소식이지만, 구체적인 수치나 원인은 제공되지 않아 이를 AI 자동화 또는 생산성 변화의 결과로 해석하기는 어렵다.
